note.explanation: An empirical formula gives the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in a compound. To get it from a molecular formula, divide all the subscripts by their greatest common factor.
examples: Hydrogen peroxide: H₂O₂ simplifies to HO.
note.checkAnswer: C₆H₆ and C₂H₂ both have the empirical formula CH.
note.simple: The molecular formula tells how many atoms are actually in a molecule. The empirical formula tells the simplest ratio between those atoms.
note.checkQuestion: What is the empirical formula of C₆H₆?
note.title: Empirical Formula
steps: Find the greatest common factor of the subscripts: 6.
Divide both subscripts by 6: C₆H₆ → CH.

mcqs.stem: What is the empirical formula of a compound with molecular formula C₂H₄?
rationales: C₂H₄ reduces to CH₂ when both subscripts are divided by 2.
C₂H₄ is the molecular formula and has not been reduced to the simplest ratio.
C₃H₆ is a different formula, not the simplest ratio of C₂H₄.
C₂H₆ has a different carbon-to-hydrogen ratio from C₂H₄.

mcqs.stem: Which is the empirical formula of hydrogen peroxide, H₂O₂?
rationales: H₂O₂ is its molecular formula, and its subscripts can both be divided by 2.
HO is the simplest whole-number ratio obtained by dividing both subscripts by 2.
H₂O has a different ratio of hydrogen to oxygen.
OH₂ has the same atom ratio as H₂O, not hydrogen peroxide.

mcqs.stem: Which pair of compounds has the same empirical formula?
rationales: C₆H₆ reduces to CH, and C₂H₂ also reduces to CH.
H₂O and H₂O₂ reduce to H₂O and HO respectively.
CO₂ and CO have different simplest atom ratios.
NH₃ and N₂H₄ reduce to different atom ratios.

mcqs.stem: Which formula shows the simplest ratio of calcium ions to fluoride ions in calcium fluoride?
rationales: CaF₂ shows the simplest 1:2 ratio of calcium to fluoride ions.
Ca₂F gives a 2:1 ratio, not the ratio in calcium fluoride.
CaF gives a 1:1 ratio, not the ratio in calcium fluoride.
Ca₂F₂ has the right ratio but is not written in its simplest form.

mcqs.stem: Which statement about water is correct?
rationales: Water's molecular formula and empirical formula are both H₂O.
HO does not give the hydrogen-to-oxygen ratio in water.
H₂O₂ is the molecular formula of hydrogen peroxide, not water.
H₄O₂ reduces to H₂O, but it is not the formula of a water molecule.

mcqs.stem: A compound has molecular formula C₆H₁₂O₆. What is its empirical formula?
rationales: C₆H₁₂O₆ is the molecular formula, and all its subscripts can be divided by 6.
Dividing the subscripts 6, 12, and 6 by 6 gives the simplest formula CH₂O.
C₂H₄O₂ can still be reduced by dividing all subscripts by 2.
C₆H₆O₆ does not have the same atom ratio as C₆H₁₂O₆.

options: An empirical formula always gives the exact number of atoms in a molecule.
Different molecular formulas can reduce to the same empirical formula.
An empirical formula is always different from a molecular formula.
Only covalent compounds can have empirical formulas.
mcqs.stem: Which statement correctly describes empirical formulas?
rationales: An empirical formula gives a simplest ratio, not necessarily the actual number of atoms.
For example, C₆H₆ and C₂H₂ both reduce to CH.
Water has the same molecular and empirical formula, so this is not always true.
The section explains that ionic compounds are represented by empirical formulas.

written.text: Give two examples of the compounds which have same empirical and molecular formulas.

rubric.why: One valid compound must be identified.
A second valid compound is needed.

modelAnswer: Water has molecular formula H₂O and empirical formula H₂O.
Ammonia has molecular formula NH₃ and empirical formula NH₃.

written.text: Find out the molecular formula of a compound whose empirical formula is CH₂O and its molar mass is 180.

rubric.why: The empirical formula mass is needed to find the multiplier.
The multiplier relates the empirical formula to the molecular formula.
rubric.description: Finds the multiplier from the molar mass.

rubric.why: Each empirical-formula subscript must be multiplied by the same multiplier.
The final molecular formula is the required answer.

modelAnswer: Multiplier = molar mass ÷ empirical formula mass = 180 ÷ 30 = 6.

written.text: Different compounds will never have the same molecule formula but they can have the same empirical formula. Explain
written.finalAnswer: A molecular formula gives the actual number of each type of atom, while an empirical formula gives only the simplest ratio. Different molecular formulas can therefore reduce to the same empirical formula; for example, benzene C₆H₆ and acetylene C₂H₂ both have empirical formula CH.

rubric.why: The answer must distinguish what a molecular formula represents.
rubric.description: Explains that a molecular formula gives the actual atom count.
rubric.how: State that it shows the actual number of each type of atom.

rubric.why: The defining feature of an empirical formula is its simplest ratio.
rubric.description: Explains what an empirical formula represents.
rubric.how: State that it gives the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms.

rubric.why: A pair of compounds illustrates the shared empirical formula.
rubric.description: Identifies benzene and acetylene as examples.
rubric.how: Give their molecular formulas C₆H₆ and C₂H₂.

rubric.why: The common empirical formula completes the explanation.
rubric.how: Show that both formulas reduce to CH.

modelAnswer: A molecular formula shows the actual number of atoms of each element in a molecule.
An empirical formula shows only the simplest whole-number ratio between the atoms.
Benzene has molecular formula C₆H₆ and acetylene has molecular formula C₂H₂.
Both have the same empirical formula, CH.

written.text: The chemical formula for sand is SiO₂ but the sand does not exist in the form of discrete molecules like H₂O. How has its formula been determined keeping in view its structure?
written.finalAnswer: Sand is represented by the empirical formula SiO₂ because its structure has silicon and oxygen atoms in the simplest 1:2 ratio; it does not represent a discrete SiO₂ molecule.

rubric.why: The answer must recognise that sand is not made of separate SiO₂ molecules.
rubric.description: Identifies the structure as not consisting of discrete molecules.
rubric.how: Explain that the formula does not stand for a separate molecule.

rubric.why: The formula represents a simplest ratio rather than a molecular unit.
rubric.description: Names SiO₂ as an empirical formula.
rubric.how: State that SiO₂ gives the simplest ratio in the structure.

rubric.why: The atom ratio explains the subscripts in the formula.
rubric.how: State that the ratio is one silicon atom to two oxygen atoms.

rubric.why: The correct formula must be stated.

modelAnswer: Sand does not exist as separate SiO₂ molecules.
Its formula represents the simplest ratio of atoms in its structure.
The ratio of silicon atoms to oxygen atoms is 1:2.
Therefore, the empirical formula of sand is SiO₂.

examTips: A short question may ask for the definition of empirical formula or for examples where the empirical and molecular formulas are the same.
For a formula-conversion question, divide every subscript by the same greatest common factor; show the division so the method earns marks.
For an explanation question, state what each formula tells you and include a suitable example such as benzene and acetylene.
Remember that an ionic compound is represented by its empirical formula, which shows the simplest ratio between its ions.

hints: Think of a compound in the section whose molecular and empirical formulas are the same.
Water is one example; choose another compound whose subscripts cannot be reduced.
yourTurn.question: Give two examples of the compounds which have same empirical and molecular formulas.
solution: The subscripts in H₂O cannot be reduced, so its empirical formula is also H₂O.
The subscripts in NH₃ cannot be reduced, so its empirical formula is also NH₃.

CH is the simplest formula that represents the ratio of carbon to hydrogen atoms.

example.question: Find the empirical formula of benzene, whose molecular formula is C₆H₆.

explain.title: Definition
explain.body: Empirical Formula of a compound shows the simplest whole number ratio of atoms present in that compound.

explain.title: Ionic compounds
explain.body: All the ionic compounds are represented by their empirical formulas. These formulas show the simplest ratio present between their ions. Calcium fluoride, CaF₂, shows the ratio present between calcium and fluoride ions in its crystal.

explain.title: Empirical and molecular formulas
explain.body: For covalent chemical compounds, which exist as molecules, the empirical formulas may be different from their molecular formulas. Hydrogen peroxide is H₂O₂ and its empirical formula is HO; benzene is C₆H₆ and its empirical formula is CH.

explain.title: Same empirical formula
explain.body: An empirical formula gives the simplest ratio, not the actual number of atoms. Benzene (C₆H₆) and acetylene (C₂H₂) both have the empirical formula CH. Water's molecular and empirical formulas are both H₂O.

mistakes: Copying the molecular formula as the empirical formula without checking whether all the subscripts can be divided by the same number.
Reducing only one subscript instead of dividing every subscript by the same greatest common factor.
Thinking that the empirical formula always tells the actual number of atoms in a molecule.
For ionic compounds, treating the formula as a discrete molecule instead of a simplest ratio between ions.
